clue.text: Father interrupting siesta for meal

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon rest
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad breaks into somebody's afternoon nap to announce lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siesta' looks like the setting of the scene, but it supplies the outer letters; the meal is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal or the food served at it.

clue.text: Without error terror's wanting just the first letter

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the opening letter alone is taken away

parts.note: fright is terror; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A pedant notes that the word terror lacks only its initial letter to be error.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites removing the T from terror, but terror must first become FRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct, that is, free of any mistake.

clue.text: American flat dweller keeping wild animals in pen with no key

indicators.note: musical keys are lettered A to G, so one such letter is dropped
keeping means holding inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: pen loses its E, a musical key

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American apartment-dweller is keeping wild animals penned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' tempts a solver toward apartments, but it means flat land: a plainsman lives on the prairie.
explanation.definitionFit: A plainsman is an inhabitant of the plains, the great flat grasslands of the American West.

clue.text: Examine 100 in hospital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A doctor checks a hundred patients on a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or examine closely.

clue.text: Naval base in estuary east of strand

indicators.note: in an across answer, east means to the right, so this piece is written after the other

parts.note: a ply is one strand of yarn or rope
an estuary is the mouth of a river

explanation.surface: Describes a navy base sited in a river estuary beside a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like a beach, but here it is a thread. Plymouth is a major Royal Navy base in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth, on the Devon coast, houses Devonport, the largest naval base in western Europe.

clue.text: After stripping blush — it's off, but all sensual

indicators.note: stripping peels away the outer layer, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: blush without its outer letters
it's without its outer letters
off without its outer letters
but without its outer letters
all without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Undressing, someone loses their blushes and becomes fully sensual.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word from blush to all is stripped of its outer letters, and what is left is joined up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustful means full of sexual desire, a strongly sensual state.

clue.text: Nocturnal bird in Middle East, a blackish songbird

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the final word

parts.note: ME is the standard abbreviation for the Middle East
taken as written
dark means blackish
the owl hunts at night

explanation.surface: A birder lists an owl, then a darker songbird, seen in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nocturnal bird' tempts a solver to take it as the definition, but the answer is the songbird at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is an American songbird of the grasslands, known for its tuneful call.

clue.text: Organ sometimes in full flow has vibration, not quiet

indicators.note: not means take away, and the crossword sign for quiet is removed

parts.note: a shudder is a shaking or vibration
sh is the call for quiet; it is removed

explanation.surface: A church organ at full volume makes the building shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ in full flow' suggests music, but it is a body part, and the flow is milk.
explanation.definitionFit: The udder is a cow's milk-producing organ, which flows freely when the animal is milked.

clue.text: Beloved idle time after a match

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment for a beloved
to moon about is to idle

explanation.surface: A sweetheart relaxing after a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game, but here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday a couple take straight after their wedding, which is a match in the marrying sense.

clue.text: Marine airmen unfortunately would need twice this rest

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
surface padding: a second word made of the same letters, which is why the clue says twice
surface padding: a comment that both words together hold two copies

explanation.surface: Seems to say servicemen will need double the usual rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter notes that marine and airmen are both rearrangements of the answer, so mixing up both words would make it twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Remain as a noun, usually plural, means what is left, the rest.

clue.text: Put in steps where there's slope around centre of path

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, holding it inside

parts.note: a grade is a gradient or slope

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle pair of letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of the four-letter word path

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying a stepped path on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to arrange in a graded series, that is, to put in stages or steps.

clue.text: Substitute colourant containing new dye, initially

indicators.note: one word holds the following letters inside itself

parts.note: a stain is a substance used to colour wood or fabric
N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of dye

explanation.surface: Suggests using a different colouring product in place of a new dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a person who takes another's place, a replacement or substitute.

clue.text: Cast can start to tire

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of tire

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark that an actor's company may begin to flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a group of actors or a verb, but here it is a noun meaning a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast in the sense of a slight shade or hue of colour is a tint.

clue.text: Reduced railway perhaps arriving at regular intervals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cut-back train timetable, with services every thirty minutes
second meaning: occurring every thirty minutes

explanation.surface: Complains about a cut-back train service that still keeps to a timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful example: a reduced train service, perhaps, runs only every thirty minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something half-hourly happens every thirty minutes, so it comes at regular intervals.

clue.text: Ruin left one in degradation

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the longer word

parts.note: demotion is degradation in rank
L is the abbreviation for left
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A disgraced figure is left alone and ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is destruction, the act of ruining a building or argument.

clue.text: Possible rescuer of one representative eagle in extremes of peril?

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the outer pair of letters
the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: first letter of peril
Roman numeral one
a Member of Parliament is an elected representative
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword staple
last letter of peril

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a lone politician, or an eagle, might save someone in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel is the hero of Baroness Orczy's novels who rescues aristocrats from the guillotine; the question mark flags that a pimpernel is only possibly a rescuer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional Scarlet Pimpernel was a daring rescuer, so a pimpernel is a possible rescuer, though the word also names a flower.

clue.text: One pulling strings to raise favourite in noble's protection

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the noble
protection suggests being sheltered within something, so the pieces are enclosed

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
to up something is to raise it
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A schemer advances their protégé under an aristocrat's patronage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling strings' suggests using influence; literally it is a person working a marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppeteer operates puppets by pulling their strings, and figuratively controls others secretly.

clue.text: Big number getting to game

parts.note: a lot is a large number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large crowd heading to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, and also a name for lotteries.

clue.text: I throw in common fossil

indicators.note: in places the opening words inside the word for common

parts.note: trite means common, hackneyed
taken as written
to lob is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone tosses an everyday fossil into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common fossil' reads as one phrase, but common is the outer word and fossil alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilobite is an extinct marine arthropod, among the most familiar fossils.

clue.text: Keen on following performance, initially patchy

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the other one
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of performance
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A fan admits their enthusiasm for a show that was uneven at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinto describes a horse with irregular patches of colour, so it is a word for patchy or piebald.

clue.text: A person is upset to see slander

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed to find they are being badmouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty in the surface but is really part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging or slanderous remark about someone's reputation.

clue.text: Complaint has large crew confined to island

indicators.note: confined to means shut inside, so the first pieces go within the island

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, such as in the Thames
L is the abbreviation for large
the crew are the men

explanation.surface: A grumble from a big ship's crew stuck on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Sort of iron age bird?

parts.note: pig iron is crude iron from a blast furnace
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: Asks what bird belongs to the Iron Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron age' looks like a period of prehistory, but iron and age are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common plump bird found in towns and cities.

clue.text: Unusual life study of former wife and poor igloo boy

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: poor here means badly made or in bad shape, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange research project about a man's ex-wife and an unfortunate lad in an igloo.
explanation.definitionFit: Exobiology is the science of possible life beyond Earth, a most unusual kind of life to study.

clue.text: Old coppers of Brixton or Lambeth implicated at the beginning

indicators.note: the beginning of each word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: South London policemen of the past were caught up in wrongdoing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers suggests police in Brixton and Lambeth, districts of south London, but means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboli, or obols, were ancient Greek coins of small value, old coins like British coppers.

clue.text: Like takeaway food in African country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: food ordered to be carried out, in the American phrase
second meaning: the West African state

explanation.surface: Seems to compare a nation's cuisine with fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food 'to go' is food packed to carry away, and Togo is a republic on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Colour of mineral containing elements of hydrocarbons

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ore is a mineral source of metal
hydrocarbons consist of carbon and hydrogen, chemical symbols C and H

explanation.surface: Describes the hue of a mineral rich in oil compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth colour, originally from a natural pigment.

clue.text: Tipping at work

parts.note: taken as written
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Suggests leaving gratuities in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' looks like giving a gratuity, but means forming the tip or top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atop another thing sits on its top, as snow tipping a peak.

clue.text: Wearing face protection reversed covers middle of eye

indicators.note: the word for face protection is written backwards
to cover the middle of something is to lie over its centre and hide it, so one piece takes the place of the central letter

parts.note: a visor shields the face
taken as written; its middle letter is the one covered

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a visor the wrong way round, so it shields their eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of EYE, the Y, is covered over by the back-to-front ROSIV, leaving E-ROSIV-E. 'Wearing' looks like having clothes on but means gradually eroding.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosive describes something that wears things away, as wind or water wears down rock.

clue.text: Bird round most of closely observed habitats initially

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
strict means closely observed, as a rule; its final T is dropped

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of habitats

explanation.surface: A naturalist watching birds near their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large flightless African bird.

clue.text: Catch again in rule playing tie

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket or football rule about taking a second chance in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' reads like a sporting catch but means to catch fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To reignite is to set alight a second time, as a fire catches again.

clue.text: Species present in area

parts.note: sp. is the standard abbreviation for species
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A wildlife survey recording which species occur locally.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field or area of activity or influence.
